newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Rep offers aid bill for crumbling schools.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Rep offers aid bill for crumbling schools.

text.p: U.S. Rep. William Clay introduced a bill to provide an additional $750 million in federal dollars to distressed school districts to tackle crumbling buildings, low test scores and other top problems.
Among their options, localities could use some of the funds to leverage bond issuance for school construction and renovation, a congressional aide said.

President Clinton already called for legislation earlier this year that would provide $5 billion over four years to help states and localities finance $20 billion in repairs and construction of public schools.

Under Clinton's plan, which faces an uphill battle on Capitol Hill, states and localities could use the federal leveraging dollars to subsidize up to half of the interest costs on tax-exempt school construction bonds.

Under Clay's bill, communities would petition the President for funding, provide evidence of a school district's problems and present a rehabilitation plan, said U.S. Rep. Carolyn McCarthy, D-N.Y., a cosponsor of Clay's bill.
Clay is a Democrat from Missouri.
